content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint analysis not fully specified",
      "quote": "For comparison of dupilumab treatment to placebo, the following hypothesis of the primary endpoint will be tested:",
      "page": 84,
      "section": "11.1 Statistical Hypothesis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The statistical methods section does not describe the specific analysis method (e.g., Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel, logistic regression) for the primary endpoint, nor the handling of missing data or stratification factors.",
      "fix": "Add a detailed description of the primary analysis method, including model, covariates, and missing data handling."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing estimand attributes for primary endpoint",
      "quote": "Proportion of patients achieving an IGA (hand and foot) score of 0 or 1 at week 16",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.1 Primary Endpoint",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The estimand for the primary endpoint lacks explicit definition of the population (e.g., FAS), the variable (IGA score), the intercurrent events strategy (e.g., how to handle patients who discontinue or use rescue medication), and the summary measure (proportion).",
      "fix": "Define the estimand attributes in the protocol or SAP, including intercurrent event handling strategies."
    },
    {
      "title": "No analysis specified for several secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "Percent change from baseline to week 16 in weekly average of daily hand and foot peak Pain NRS",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The statistical methods section does not describe analyses for many secondary endpoints (e.g., Pain NRS, Sleep NRS, percent surface area, HECSI, QOLHEQ, WPAI/CIQ). Only the primary and key secondary are mentioned in the hypothesis.",
      "fix": "Provide analysis methods for all secondary endpoints, including model, covariates, and missing data handling."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of multiplicity for secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "Secondary Endpoints for Efficacy:",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not describe how to control the family-wise error rate for multiple secondary endpoints. Without a hierarchical testing procedure or other adjustment, the risk of false positives is high.",
      "fix": "Specify a multiplicity control strategy (e.g., hierarchical testing, Bonferroni) for secondary endpoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size assumption inconsistent with observed effect",
      "quote": "The assumed treatment difference of 24% is based on the effect of 26% observed in dupilumab phase 3 monotherapy studies in adult patients with AD and adjusted to account for the potential inclusion of some patients with ACD who would be missed with certain patch testing (ie, TRUE test) at screening.",
      "page": 85,
      "section": "11.2 Justification of Sample Size",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "advisory",
      "explanation": "The sample size justification uses a 24% difference, but the observed effect is 26% and the adjustment for ACD is not quantified. This may be acceptable but should be clarified to ensure the assumed effect is realistic.",
      "fix": "Provide a quantitative basis for the adjustment from 26% to 24%."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for exploratory endpoints",
      "quote": "In patients with AD lesions on other parts of the body in addition to hands and feet;",
      "page": 41,
      "section": "4.1.4 Exploratory Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Exploratory endpoints (EASI, IGA, EASI-75) are listed but no statistical analysis methods are described for them in the statistical plan.",
      "fix": "Add a brief description of analyses for exploratory endpoints, even if descriptive."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of missing data for endpoints",
      "quote": "Handling of missing data due to the COVID-19 pandemic and any additional analyses required to investigate the impact of COVID-19 to understand estimated treatment effect and safety will be detailed in the SAP.",
      "page": 84,
      "section": "11 STATISTICAL PLAN",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol only mentions missing data handling for COVID-19, but does not specify general missing data methods (e.g., multiple imputation, mixed model repeated measures) for primary and secondary endpoints.",
      "fix": "Specify the primary missing data handling approach for all efficacy endpoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent sample size statement",
      "quote": "Approximately 130 patients (65 patients per arm) will be enrolled at approximately 50 global sites.",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "7.1 Number of Patients Planned",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The sample size section says 130 patients, but the cap on adults (100) and hands-only (100) may lead to fewer than 130 if enrollment is not met. This is not necessarily inconsistent but should be clarified.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether the caps are targets or maximums and how they affect the total sample size."
    }
  ]
}
